title: Flow through granular filter columns
bodyMd:
Water was passed through columns filled to the same height with four granular materials. Each column had the same diameter. The water pressure above each column was held constant. Particle diameter refers to the grains making up the column, not to contaminants in the water. The measured flow rate is the volume passing through per minute after steady flow was established. Removed fraction is the percentage of incoming test particles retained by that column. Equal incoming particle concentrations were used.

| Grain diameter (mm) | Flow rate (mL/min) | Removed fraction (%) |
|---:|---:|---:|
|0.5|20|95|
|1.0|40|80|
|2.0|70|60|
|4.0|100|35|

The team defines an acceptable column as one that passes at least35mL/min and removes at least75% of the incoming test particles. Estimates within the table may use straight-line interpolation, but no relation outside the tested grain sizes has been established.
